name: Page banners
summary: Four banners for the top of a page or section (info, success, warning and error), each with a bold first phrase, one sentence and one action.
use: for news about the whole page or account that should stay until it's handled or dismissed
a11y: Info, success and warning are polite status regions; the error is an alert and can't be dismissed until it's fixed; dismiss buttons are named after their banner, and focus moves to the next banner.

use_when: something affects the whole page or account and stays true until it's handled
avoid_when: a quick confirmation of something the person just did: use toast-undo
a problem with one field: use field-error
the whole page can't load: use page-error

parts.name: banners.title
parts.what: the heading: what happened, in plain words, as in “New: approval rules.”

parts.name: banners.message
parts.what: one or two sentences: what it means and what to do next, as in “Bills over $5,000 now need a second approver.”

empty.how: the Smart UI renderer puts one plain 'Nothing to show yet.' line in an empty list

loading.how: the Smart UI renderer draws each marked slot as a quiet block of its size while the data arrives; the static file shows the filled part

error.how: The error banner is an alert and stays until the problem is fixed.

disabled.how: No control here is ever disabled; each one always does something.

overflow.how: Text wraps beside the icon; the action follows the sentence.

long_text.how: Titles balance and body text wraps at word boundaries inside a capped measure.

keyboard: Tab reaches each banner's action, then its dismiss button
Dismissing moves focus to the next banner
